</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-layer Distillation and Optimization Challenges</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Early studies on knowledge distillation have shown that supervising multiple intermediate layers can lead to more effective knowledge transfer. Methods such as <span id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Patient Knowledge Distillation</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, <span id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ReviewKD</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, and recent feature-dynamics-based approaches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gong et al., 2025</a>)</cite> demonstrate the benefits of multi-layer alignment in deep networks.
To enable supervision at intermediate layers, prior methods commonly attach layer-wise <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">projectors</em> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Miles and Mikolajczyk, 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Miles et al., 2024</a>)</cite> that reconcile mismatched feature spaces before computing alignment losses.
However, extending multi-layer distillation to VLA models introduces additional challenges: gradient interference can arise among the separate projectors, which can degrade alignment quality.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Background</h3>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">VLA as student and manipulation objective.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For ease of understanding, we view representation alignment from the perspective of feature knowledge distillation.
We consider a pretrained VLA policy as the <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">student</em> model.
Given an observation (e.g., multi-view images) <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>I</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I</annotation></semantics></math> and an instruction <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>, the student induces an action policy <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
One possible instantiation is an autoregressive policy  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2024</a>)</cite> that predicts an action sequence <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=\{a_{t}\}_{t=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=\{a_{t}\}_{t=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}\!\left(\,\cdot\mid I,P,a_{&lt;t}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}\!\left(\,\cdot\mid I,P,a_{&lt;t}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">while our method is agnostic to the specific action parameterization (e.g., continuous regression or discretized action tokens).
The student is trained with an action learning loss</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}=\mathcal{L}\!\left(A,A^{gt}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>action</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.520em;" width="0.520em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}=\mathcal{L}\!\left(A,A^{gt}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A^{gt}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A^{gt}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the ground-truth action sequence from demonstrations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">3D vision foundation model as teacher.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We assume access to a <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">frozen</em> 3D-aware vision foundation model as the <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">teacher</em>, which provides geometry-grounded <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">patch token</em> representations.
Such models (e.g., VGGT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, Depth Anything 3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>) learn spatially consistent features from monocular or multi-view images and can serve as strong supervision signals for injecting 3D cues into a VLA student’s visual representations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Single-layer representation alignment.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Single-layer alignment applies supervision on the <em id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">visual tokens</em> of a student model by matching them to a teacher’s intermediate representations at a selected depth to improve spatial awareness.
There has been a line of prior work adopting single-layer intermediate feature matching, which is simple yet effective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Let <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{S}_{s}(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{S}_{s}(\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{S}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{T}_{\tau}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>τ</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{T}_{\tau}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the student/teacher vision representations at student layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and teacher layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.
SF aligns one student layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> to one teacher layer <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\{s^{\star}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\{s^{\star}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}=\{\tau^{\star}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}=\{\tau^{\star}\}</annotation></semantics></math>) via a lightweight projector <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and optimizes</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}=\ell\!\left(p_{\phi}\!\left(h^{S}_{s^{\star}}(\theta)\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau^{\star}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.247em;" width="0.247em"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msup><mi>τ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}=\ell\!\left(p_{\phi}\!\left(h^{S}_{s^{\star}}(\theta)\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau^{\star}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> can be any similarity-based loss.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Accordingly, most representation-alignment methods optimize a joint objective:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{total}}\;=\;\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}\;+\;\lambda\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>total</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>action</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{total}}\;=\;\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}\;+\;\lambda\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> balances task learning and representation alignment.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment</h3>

<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">From single-layer to multi-layer alignment: richer cues, but no gains in practice.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Despite its effectiveness, single-layer alignment has limitations: (i) <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">single-point</em> alignment requires post-hoc layer selection, and (ii) it fails to use complementary cross-layer signals.
A natural extension is to align <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">multiple</em> layers simultaneously, since spatial cues may be distributed across depth and multi-layer distillation is effective in other settings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Skean et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Concretely, given ordered layer lists <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\{s_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\{s_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> (student) and <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}=\{\tau_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}=\{\tau_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> (teacher), previous multi-layer alignment methods use layer-specific projectors <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\ell\!\left(p_{\phi_{i}}\!\left(h^{S}_{s_{i}}(\theta)\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau_{i}}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.247em;" width="0.247em"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\ell\!\left(p_{\phi_{i}}\!\left(h^{S}_{s_{i}}(\theta)\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau_{i}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">However, this prior-style design <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gong et al., 2025</a>)</cite> <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hurts</em> downstream VLA manipulation performance (as shown in Fig. <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Residual-dynamical view: multi-layer alignment should be cone-to-cone, yet learned projectors decouple.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand why multi-layer alignment fails, we view both student and teacher backbones as residual dynamical systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">Weinan, 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al., 2017</a>)</cite>.
Let <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> be the student residual representation at layer <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="h_{l+1}\;=\;h_{l}\;+\;F_{l}\!\left(h_{l};\theta_{l}\right),\qquad l=0,\dots,L-1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{l+1}\;=\;h_{l}\;+\;F_{l}\!\left(h_{l};\theta_{l}\right),\qquad l=0,\dots,L-1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{l}:=F_{l}(h_{l};\theta_{l})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{l}:=F_{l}(h_{l};\theta_{l})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Empirically, the hidden states within each model tend to converge into the same feature space <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gromov et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2024</a>)</cite> (Fig. <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), consistent with the “cone effect” <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2019</a>)</cite>.
This suggests multi-layer alignment should learn a consistent <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cone-to-cone</em> mapping from the student residual stream to the teacher residual stream.
Yet, under naive multi-layer alignment, the learned projectors <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">diverge</em> and become nearly orthogonal in parameter space (Please refer to Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Projector Similarity ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>), indicating that different depths follow inconsistent alignment paths rather than sharing a coherent mapping.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/grad.png" id="S3.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:238/196;" width="238" height="196" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.F1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine similarity between gradients induced by different alignment losses in the VLA’s shallow layers.
<span id="S3.F1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B30000;">Red</span> indicates gradient coherence, while <span id="S3.F1.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000B3;">Blue</span> indicates gradient interference. Detailed results are provided in Fig. <a href="#A8.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Consequence for gradient stability. ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> and Fig. <a href="#A8.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Consequence for gradient stability. ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Corollary: early-layer updates are a superposition of future local distillation gradients.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Why do inconsistent projectors matter for optimization?
Our key observation is that in a Pre-LN residual stream, back-propagation through depth is close to identity when residual updates are small, so an early-layer representation receives an <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">additive</em> mixture of gradient signals coming from <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">all</em> aligned future layers.
Formally, Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> derives (Corollary 1) that for an early layer <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E7X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\nabla_{h_{i}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\nabla_{h_{i}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,\underbrace{J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l}}_{=:~v_{l}}+\mathcal{E}_{i}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo></mstyle><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>α</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.548em">:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,\underbrace{J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l}}_{=:~v_{l}}+\mathcal{E}_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E7Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle g_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle g_{l}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E7Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle:=\nabla_{z_{l}}\ell(z_{l},t_{l}),\qquad z_{l}=p_{\phi_{l}}(h_{l})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo lspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=\nabla_{z_{l}}\ell(z_{l},t_{l}),\qquad z_{l}=p_{\phi_{l}}(h_{l}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">transport error</em> controlled by residual-smallness and <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the layer-wise weight.
Thus, <span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">whether multi-layer alignment helps hinges on whether <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{v_{l}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{v_{l}\}</annotation></semantics></math> add constructively or cancel.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proposition: Jacobian-induced gradient interference under multiple independent projectors.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G\approx\sum_{l\geq i}\alpha_{l}v_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">≈</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G\approx\sum_{l\geq i}\alpha_{l}v_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the superposed gradient (ignoring <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>).
Its squared norm expands as</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|G\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{l}\alpha_{l}^{2}\|v_{l}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{a\neq b}\alpha_{a}\alpha_{b}\,\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>l</mi></munder><mrow><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|G\|_{2}^{2}=\sum_{l}\alpha_{l}^{2}\|v_{l}\|_{2}^{2}+\sum_{a\neq b}\alpha_{a}\alpha_{b}\,\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the cross terms determine constructive vs. destructive interference.
Crucially, each cross term is a bilinear form on teacher-side error signals:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle=g_{a}^{\top}\underbrace{\left(J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})\,J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}\right)}_{=:~\mathcal{M}_{ab}}g_{b}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.548em">:</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></munder><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle=g_{a}^{\top}\underbrace{\left(J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})\,J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}\right)}_{=:~\mathcal{M}_{ab}}g_{b}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">With <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">multiple independent</em> projectors, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ab}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ab}</annotation></semantics></math> is <em id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.3.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not structurally coupled</em> across <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math>:
the interaction matrix <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> need not be symmetric or positive semidefinite (PSD), and can vary arbitrarily across layers.
As a result, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> may be weak, sign-unstable, or even destructive.
Empirically, we observe that cross-layer alignment gradients remain poorly aligned (small pairwise cosine similarity) throughout training (Shown in the upper part of Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Residual-dynamical view: multi-layer alignment should be cone-to-cone, yet learned projectors decouple. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), consistent with gradient conflict under unconstrained cross terms.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Motivation</h3>

<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Shared projector yields a structured decomposition and improves gradient coherence in practice.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multi-layer alignment with multiple <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">independent</em> projectors often underperforms due to gradient interference across layers.
In contrast, if we <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">share a single projector</em> across layers (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{l}\equiv\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{l}\equiv\phi</annotation></semantics></math>), Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>
shows that although <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ab}=J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{b})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ab}=J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{b})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> is not necessarily symmetric or PSD,
it can be decomposed into a <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">common PSD reference</em> plus a controlled deviation:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E10"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}&amp;=g_{a}^{\top}\mathcal{M}_{ab}g_{b}=g_{a}^{\top}Mg_{b}+\Delta_{ab},\\
&amp;\qquad M:=JJ^{\top}\succeq 0.\end{aligned}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>share</mi></msub></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>⪰</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}&amp;=g_{a}^{\top}\mathcal{M}_{ab}g_{b}=g_{a}^{\top}Mg_{b}+\Delta_{ab},\\
&amp;\qquad M:=JJ^{\top}\succeq 0.\end{aligned}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Moreover, on the error-signal subspace <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}=\mathrm{span}\{g_{l}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>span</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}=\mathrm{span}\{g_{l}\}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is near-isometric, we obtain the
signal-aligned lower bound (Theorem <a href="#A8.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem H.1 (Shared projector induces coherent cross-layer interference under Pre-LN transport). ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H.1</span></a>):</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}\;\geq\;c\,g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}\;-\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|g_{a}\|_{2}^{2}+\|g_{b}\|_{2}^{2}}{2}\;-\;|\Delta_{ab}|" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>share</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}\;\geq\;c\,g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}\;-\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|g_{a}\|_{2}^{2}+\|g_{b}\|_{2}^{2}}{2}\;-\;|\Delta_{ab}|</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">for constants <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
When <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> is typically positive and the deviation terms are small, sharing biases cross-layer gradients
toward constructive interference.
We validate this prediction by visualizing gradient angles: with a shared projector, cross-layer gradient cosine similarities
increase substantially compared to the independent-projector baseline (Shown in the lower part of Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Residual-dynamical view: multi-layer alignment should be cone-to-cone, yet learned projectors decouple. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>),
and this improved coherence translates into significant downstream gains on VLA manipulation tasks
(Fig. <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
This motivates <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>’s design choice: <em id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">share the projector</em> to reduce gradient conflict and make multi-layer alignment effective.
Full proofs and additional empirical analysis are provided in Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Methodology</h2>

<figure id="S4.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/Overview_final.png" id="S4.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/235;" width="429" height="235" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F2.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S4.F2.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> Overview of <span id="S4.F2.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>. On the <span id="S4.F2.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">left</span>, we select a sample from LIBERO to showcase <span id="S4.F2.8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>’s performance. On the <span id="S4.F2.8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">right</span>, we use the outputs from VGGT layers <math id="S4.F2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{1,3,9,15,21\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.110em" minsize="1.110em">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{1,3,9,15,21\}</annotation></semantics></math> to directly predict the depth map, demonstrating that different layers contain rich 3D information. Some of the illustrations were generated by GPT-4o <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hurst et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Overview of <span id="S4.SS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>, a multi-layer representation alignment method on the residual stream.
As shown in Fig. <a href="#S4.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> has three key designs:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i) Multi-layer representation alignment.</span>
Single-layer alignment cannot fully leverage the rich semantic information across layers and often relies on post-hoc layer selection.
<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> aligns multiple layers, and Sec. <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Criteria for Layer Selection ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a> shows that with a simple layer selection strategy, <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> outperforms the baselines.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii) Shared projector to reduce gradient conflict.</span>
Naive multi-layer alignment may cause gradient conflicts across layers.
<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> uses a <em id="S4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">shared</em> projector to learn a common mapping between two residual streams.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iii) Matryoshka-style activation for balancing depths.</span>
As indicated by Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ Corollary: early-layer updates are a superposition of future local distillation gradients. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, gradients from multiple alignment losses approximately add up, so shallow layers receive denser supervision.
Our experiments also show that shallow layers are easier to align (Please refer to Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Why We Need a Nested Sparse-Activation Mechanism to Balance Multiple Alignment Losses ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a> for more details).
To prevent shallow layers from dominating the shared projector, <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> introduces a Matryoshka-style <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kusupati et al., 2022</a>)</cite> parameter-sparse activation mechanism, which progressively increases the activated parameter fraction from shallow to deep layers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow the multi-layer alignment setting in Sec. <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, with <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> aligned layer pairs
<math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(s_{i},\tau_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(s_{i},\tau_{i})\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> and the corresponding hidden states <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(h^{S}_{s_{i}},h^{T}_{\tau_{i}})\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(h^{S}_{s_{i}},h^{T}_{\tau_{i}})\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Crucially, we replace the layer-specific projectors <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{\phi_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. <a href="#S3.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ From single-layer to multi-layer alignment: richer cues, but no gains in practice. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> with a single shared projector <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\Phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\Phi}</annotation></semantics></math>,
which learns a <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">shared</em> student-to-teacher mapping that is consistent across depth.
For the detailed layer selection strategy, please refer to Sec.<a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Optimal Number of Alignment Layers ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a> and Sec. <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Criteria for Layer Selection ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<tr id="S4.T2.fig2.3.1.6" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">
