<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Matryoshka-style Sparse Activation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We parameterize a single shared projector
<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\Phi}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{S}}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\Phi}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{S}}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}}</annotation></semantics></math> with a maximum internal width <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>.
Specifically, we present a two-layer MLP projector:</p>
<table id="S4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\Phi}(x)=W_{2}\,\sigma(W_{1}x),W_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_{S}},\;W_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}\times m}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\Phi}(x)=W_{2}\,\sigma(W_{1}x),W_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_{S}},\;W_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{T}\times m},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is a pointwise nonlinearity (e.g., GELU), and <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each aligned layer <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we activate only the <em id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">first</em> <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> hidden channels of the shared projector, where <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> increases monotonically with depth.
By default, we use a simple linear width schedule:</p>
<table id="S4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i}=\rho_{\min}+(\rho_{\max}-\rho_{\min})\cdot\frac{i-1}{\max(N-1,\,1)},m_{i}\;=\;\left\lceil\rho_{i}\,m\right\rceil," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mo>⌈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>⌉</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i}=\rho_{\min}+(\rho_{\max}-\rho_{\min})\cdot\frac{i-1}{\max(N-1,\,1)},m_{i}\;=\;\left\lceil\rho_{i}\,m\right\rceil,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\min}=0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\min}=0.2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\max}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\max}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is the maximum hidden width of the shared projector.
When <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1</annotation></semantics></math>, this reduces to <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{1}=\rho_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{1}=\rho_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., activating the full projector). Equivalently, define a binary gating vector <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}\in\{0,1\}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}\in\{0,1\}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math> as a prefix mask</p>
<table id="S4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E14.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g_{i}[j]\;=\;\mathbb{I}\!\left(j\leq m_{i}\right),\qquad j=1,\dots,m," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>j</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mi>𝕀</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}[j]\;=\;\mathbb{I}\!\left(j\leq m_{i}\right),\qquad j=1,\dots,m,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">and apply it to the hidden activation:</p>
<table id="S4.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\Phi}^{(i)}(x)=W_{2}\!\left(g_{i}\odot\sigma(W_{1}x)\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\Phi}^{(i)}(x)=W_{2}\!\left(g_{i}\odot\sigma(W_{1}x)\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> denotes element-wise multiplication.
This construction yields a <em id="S4.SS3.p2.4.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Matryoshka</em> (nested) family of projectors
<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{\Phi}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{\Phi}^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> that share parameters, but expose increasing effective capacity for deeper layers.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training objective.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our final training objective combines the task loss for action prediction with the proposed multi-layer alignment regularizer:</p>
<table id="S4.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\textbf{{{ROCKET}} }}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}+\lambda\,\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\ell\!\left(p_{\Phi}^{(i)}\!\left(h^{S}_{s_{i}}\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau_{i}}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">ROCKET</mtext><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold"> </mtext></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>action</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.247em;" width="0.247em"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\textbf{{{ROCKET}} }}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}+\lambda\,\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\ell\!\left(p_{\Phi}^{(i)}\!\left(h^{S}_{s_{i}}\right),\,h^{T}_{\tau_{i}}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>action</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{action}}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E2" title="Equation 2 ‣ VLA as student and manipulation objective. ‣ 3.1 Background ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), and
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> balances task learning and representation alignment.
By default, we use <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(a,b)=1-\cos(a,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(a,b)=1-\cos(a,b)</annotation></semantics></math> and set <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Main Result</h2>

<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/libero_plus_dense.png" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:481/77;" width="481" height="77" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Success rate (%) on LIBERO-Plus. Results are reported under the seven perturbations defined by LIBERO-Plus. Each column shows the average success rate over four task groups: Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long. Detailed results are provided in Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Per-task Results on LIBERO-Plus ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct experiments on <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO-Plus</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fei et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Each benchmark comprises four sub-datasets (task suites). Following the official protocol of <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO-Plus</span> as well as the common practice used in <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">PI0</span>/<span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">PI0.5</span>, we mix the four sub-datasets during training and evaluate a <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">single</em> model on the four corresponding test suites. Unless otherwise specified, we fine-tune the <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">OpenVLA-7B</span> pretrained weights on <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO</span> and <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO-Plus</span>. We adopt the training setting of <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SF</span> and <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">OpenVLA-OFT</span>. Specifically, we perform LoRA fine-tuning for <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps with batch size <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>.
In addition, to compare multiple methods under the <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full fine-tuning</em> regime as in <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">PI0.5</span>, we run full fine-tuning on <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">LIBERO</span> for <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps with batch size <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RoboTwin 2.0.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow the official training protocol and perform LoRA fine-tuning for <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps with a batch size of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>. For evaluation, we follow the <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RoboTwin 2.0</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> evaluation procedure with a random seed of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, and run <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> trials for both the easy and hard task sets. We use the task subset specified in SF for both training and evaluation. For all benchmarks, we report task execution success rate (SR, %) by default.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
Success rate (%) of the PI0.5 with different representation alignment strategies
on the LIBERO.
</span></figcaption>
<table id="S5.T3.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S5.T3.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T3.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T3.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Method</span></th>
<th id="S5.T3.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T3.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Spatial</span></th>
<th id="S5.T3.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T3.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Object</span></th>
<th id="S5.T3.5.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T3.5.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Goal</span></th>
<th id="S5.T3.5.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T3.5.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Long</span></th>

</section>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Projector and Alignment Hyperparameters.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure a fair comparison, we keep the projector architecture <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">identical across all experiments</em>. In particular, we use a <em id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">single</em> projector whose structure and dimensionalities exactly match <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SF</span>.
For the alignment-loss weight <math id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> and the number of layers used by the single-layer alignment baseline in <span id="S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">SF</span>, we directly use the best configurations reported by their hyperparameter search.
More training hyperparameters and implementation details are provided in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Training Details ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Performance of <span id="S5.SS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> Across Different Settings</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LIBERO with OpenVLA-7B.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, we compare representative approaches on LIBERO, including:
(i) standard 2D VLA models, covering both direct fine-tuning of the base VLA and variants that boost performance via additional modules;
(ii) 3D VLA methods with explicit 3D inputs, including augmenting inputs with explicit 3D signals and recovering 3D structure via depth estimation; and
(iii) two single-layer representation alignment baselines.
Results show that <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> substantially outperforms prior models.
Even compared to Spatial Forcing, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> matches its performance while using only <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>4% of the compute budget (please refer to Table <a href="#S6.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 6.3 Data and Computational Efficiency ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> for more details).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LIBERO with PI0.5.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">On PI0.5, we compare <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> with the direct fine-tuning baseline and Spatial Forcing under the full fine-tuning setting.
As reported in Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ RoboTwin 2.0. ‣ 5.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 5 Main Result ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, under the same setting, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> improves performance by <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Overall, this improvement suggests that even for smaller-scale models under full fine-tuning, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> can effectively inject spatial reasoning capability.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LIBERO-Plus with OpenVLA-7B.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further evaluate <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> on LIBERO-Plus, a robustness benchmark with seven perturbation dimensions, and find that <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> is more robust under challenging spatial perturbations. As shown in Fig. <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5 Main Result ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> achieves the best average success rate (81.7%), outperforming the baseline (80.0%). Notably, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> shows the most pronounced gains under <em id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Robot</em> and <em id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Layout</em> shifts, which are strongly tied to spatial geometry rather than appearance. These improvements suggest that <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> enhances spatial reasoning instead of relying on positional shortcuts.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RoboTwin 2.0 with PI0.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For bimanual tasks, we evaluate on RoboTwin 2.0 using ALOHA assets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Aldaco et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
As shown in Fig. <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ RoboTwin 2.0 with PI0. ‣ 5.2 Performance of ROCKET Across Different Settings ‣ 5 Main Result ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> achieves a clear advantage in the Easy setting, while in the Hard setting it is only slightly behind the strongest baseline (finetuned).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/robotwin.png" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:481/82;" width="481" height="82" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Success rate (%) on RoboTwin 2.0 (ALOHA) under Easy and Hard settings across five bimanual tasks, comparing <span id="S5.F6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> with DP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chi et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, RDT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and PI0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Discussion</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Optimal Number of Alignment Layers</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A key design choice in multi-layer alignment is the number of aligned layer pairs.
To ensure a fair comparison, we fix the projector capacity and study how many layers should be aligned under a fixed-size projector.
Following the strategy in  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2019</a>)</cite>, we uniformly sample <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> layers from the VLA LLM backbone and <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> layers from VGGT, and align them as <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> layer pairs.
As shown in Table <a href="#S6.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 6.1 Optimal Number of Alignment Layers ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, aligning roughly <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> layer pairs yields the best trade-off, and performance saturates or degrades beyond this range.
Therefore, <span id="S6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> uses <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=10</annotation></semantics></math> aligned layer pairs by default in all experiments.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S6.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The impact of the number of aligned layers on final performance, evaluated on LIBERO.</span></figcaption>

</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Criteria for Layer Selection</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We investigate several layer selection strategies. We apply the same strategy to select the same layers for both VGGT and VLA. Specifically, we consider:
(i) the <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Uniform</span> sampling strategy in Sec. <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Optimal Number of Alignment Layers ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>;
(ii) selecting <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> layers separately from the <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Shallow</span>, <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Middle</span>, and <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Deep</span> stages;
(iii) <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">E2M-Last1</span>: uniformly sampling from early-to-middle layers and additionally including the last layer; and
(iv) two importance-based heuristics: Motivated by the hypothesis that layers with higher input–output cosine similarity are less informative <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gromov et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, we design two similarity-based criteria.
Specifically, the first criterion computes the cosine similarity between the input and output representations aggregated over windows of <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> consecutive Transformer blocks; <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Sim-1-Top</span> selects the <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> layers with the highest similarity, while <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Sim-1-Last</span> selects those with the lowest similarity.
The second one computes similarity per block; <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Sim-2-Top</span> selects the <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> highest-similarity layers, whereas <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Sim-2-Last</span> selects the <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> lowest-similarity layers.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Results in Table <a href="#S6.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 6.2 Criteria for Layer Selection ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> show that even without expensive post-hoc search, most reasonable selection strategies provide consistent gains, suggesting that <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> is robust to layer choice.
Unless otherwise stated, we adopt the <span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">E2M-Last1</span> strategy as the default setting.
Implementation details and the exact layer indices are provided in Appendix <a href="#A9.SS1" title="I.1 Similarity-based Layer Selection ‣ Appendix I Details of Layer Selection Strategies ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I.1</span></a>, <a href="#A9.SS2" title="I.2 Detailed Chosen indices for All Layer Selection Strategies ‣ Appendix I Details of Layer Selection Strategies ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Data and Computational Efficiency</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the efficiency of <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> from three perspectives:
<span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i) Limited-data training.</span>
Using <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> random subsets of LIBERO (each trained for <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math>k steps), Table <a href="#S6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 6.3 Data and Computational Efficiency ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows that <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> still achieves strong performance, indicating high data efficiency, which is particularly important in robotics where data collection is costly.
<span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii) Convergence speed.</span>
In Fig. <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> outperforms the baseline by <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>10% at around <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>k steps and continues to improve thereafter, suggesting that the proposed multi-level alignment mechanism more effectively exploits spatial cues across different layers. Please refer to Table <a href="#A2.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Appendix B Performance Trajectories on LIBERO Across Training ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> for the complete results.
<span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iii) Computational cost to reach SOTA.</span>
Table <a href="#S6.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 6.3 Data and Computational Efficiency ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> summarizes the compute overhead of same-sized models reported in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Multi-layer Alignment with Shared Projector ‣ 4 Methodology ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. <span id="S6.SS3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> reaches SOTA performance while the previous best method incurs <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="24\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24\times</annotation></semantics></math> higher cost, demonstrating strong overall computational efficiency among post-training methods.</p>
</div>

<td id="S6.T7.6.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:9.8pt;padding-right:9.8pt;"><math id="S6.T7.m16" class="ltx_Math" style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" alttext="1\times 32\times 50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" mathbackground="#D6D6D6" mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" lspace="0.222em" mathbackground="#D6D6D6" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" mathbackground="#D6D6D6" mathsize="0.900em">32</mn><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" lspace="0.222em" mathbackground="#D6D6D6" mathsize="0.900em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;" mathbackground="#D6D6D6" mathsize="0.900em">50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\times 32\times 50</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S6.T7.6.8.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#D6D6D6;">k</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Ablation Study</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate the key components of <span id="S6.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>.
Introducing multi-layer alignment with <em id="S6.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">independent</em> projectors degrades performance to <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating gradient interference across layers.
Replacing independent projectors with the proposed <em id="S6.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">shared</em> projector improves performance to <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
Finally, adding the Matryoshka-style sparse activation further increases performance to <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S6.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="S6.T8.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Ablation study of <span id="S6.T8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> on LIBERO.</span></figcaption>

</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>, a residual-oriented multi-layer representation alignment framework that transfers 3D spatial priors from a strong vision foundation model into 2D-pretrained VLA models. By using a <em id="S7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">layer-invariant shared projector</em>, <span id="S7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> mitigates gradient interference that arises in naïve multi-layer distillation, and our Matryoshka-style sparse activation further balances supervision across depths. Extensive experiments show that <span id="S7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> consistently improves spatial grounding and generalization across datasets and VLA backbones, achieving near state-of-the-art performance on LIBERO with only a small fraction of the compute. We hope <span id="S7.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> offers a simple and scalable route to more reliable 3D-aware robotic manipulation.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of Machine
Learning and Embodied AI. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none
which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Training Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Teacher Freezing.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Throughout the entire training pipeline, we keep the teacher model frozen and only fine-tune the student VLA model.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learning Rate Schedule and Batch Size.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">OpenVLA-7B</span> for a total of <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps, following its default learning-rate decay strategy with a minor adjustment: we keep the learning rate at <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> for the first <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps, and then decay it to <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> for the remainder of training. We use a batch size of 32.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For the search-oriented experiments in Sec. <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 Optimal Number of Alignment Layers ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>, Sec. <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Criteria for Layer Selection ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a> and Table <a href="#S6.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 6.3 Data and Computational Efficiency ‣ 6 Discussion ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, to reduce computational cost we decrease the batch size to 16. Meanwhile, to avoid under-training, we keep the learning rate at <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> for the first <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> steps and then decay it to <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math> afterwards.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">PI-Model Experiments.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For experiments related to PI0.5, we set the batch size to 64 and train the model in PyTorch; all other settings follow the default configuration.
For PI0 experiments on <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RoboTwin 2.0</span>, we use a batch size of 16 and train with the JAX implementation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We also observe that in such single-task settings, the action loss typically converges quickly. Therefore, we reduce the coefficient of the alignment loss from its default value of 0.5 to 0.125, which yields strong empirical performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Performance Trajectories on LIBERO Across Training</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Appendix B Performance Trajectories on LIBERO Across Training ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> reports success rates on the four LIBERO suites (Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long) at different training stages, together with the overall average. Unlike single-point evaluation at the end of training, this table highlights performance trajectories over the full training course, enabling a more complete comparison of training dynamics across methods.</p>
</div>

<th id="A2.T9.11.18.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="A2.T9.11.18.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">10k</span></th>
<td id="A2.T9.11.18.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A2.T9.11.18.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">90.8</span></td>

<td id="A2.T9.11.20.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A2.T9.11.20.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">96.0</span></td>
