</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Dataset Details</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>LIBERO</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LIBERO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> is a benchmark suite for language-conditioned robotic manipulation, designed to evaluate multi-task imitation learning and generalization. The original LIBERO release consists of <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">12</span> manipulation tasks grouped into <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">4</span> task suites, instantiated across <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3</span> robot embodiments. Tasks are defined with natural language instructions, enabling direct study of vision-language-action (VLA) policy learning.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The four task suites capture complementary generalization axes. LIBERO-SPATIAL focuses on spatial configuration variation, LIBERO-OBJECT emphasizes object-level diversity, LIBERO-GOAL introduces goal variation within shared task structures, and LIBERO-LONG contains long-horizon, multi-stage manipulation tasks requiring sequential reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. This structured design enables controlled evaluation of cross-task and cross-goal generalization.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">LIBERO provides expert demonstration trajectories collected in simulation using RoboSuite. The original dataset contains approximately <span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">20,000</span> demonstration episodes in total, with each task comprising roughly <span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">1,500–2,000</span> trajectories depending on task complexity. Each episode consists of temporally dense state-action sequences spanning hundreds of timesteps.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Each episode includes synchronized multimodal observations, including RGB images from fixed camera viewpoints and robot proprioceptive states such as joint positions and gripper status. Actions are specified in continuous control space, typically as end-effector pose commands. Data are stored in a standardized trajectory format, facilitating efficient loading and integration with common imitation learning pipelines.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>LIBERO-Plus</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LIBERO-Plus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fei et al., 2025</a>)</cite> is an extended version of the original LIBERO benchmark, designed to scale up task diversity and data volume while preserving the same language-conditioned manipulation setting. LIBERO-Plus significantly expands the number of tasks and demonstrations, enabling evaluation of large-capacity vision-language-action (VLA) models under more data-rich and heterogeneous training regimes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Compared to the original LIBERO benchmark, LIBERO-Plus includes <span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">over 100</span> manipulation tasks spanning a broader range of object configurations, goal specifications, and scene layouts. Tasks are defined using natural language instructions and are organized to support both multi-task learning and compositional generalization. The expanded task set increases structural and semantic diversity, making LIBERO-Plus more suitable for training and evaluating foundation-scale robotic policies.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">LIBERO-Plus provides a substantially larger collection of expert demonstration trajectories generated in simulation. In total, the dataset contains <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">hundreds of thousands of demonstration episodes</span>, with each task comprising thousands of trajectories. Each episode consists of temporally dense state-action sequences, supporting long-horizon policy learning and sequence modeling.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Each episode includes synchronized multimodal observations, including RGB visual inputs, robot proprioceptive states, and continuous control actions specified in end-effector space. Data are stored in the same standardized trajectory format as LIBERO, enabling seamless reuse of training pipelines and direct comparison across LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>RoboTwin 2.0</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">RoboTwin 2.0 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> is a large-scale simulation benchmark and dataset for bimanual robotic manipulation, providing both an automated data generator and unified evaluation protocols. The official release instantiates <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">50 dual-arm tasks</span> across <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5 robot embodiments</span>, targeting robust long-horizon manipulation with diverse object interactions. RoboTwin 2.0 is built on an annotated object library (RoboTwin-OD) containing <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">731 object instances</span> spanning <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">147 categories</span>, enabling systematic task variation in object geometry, placement, and scene composition.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to the generator, RoboTwin 2.0 provides <span id="A3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">over 100,000</span> pre-collected expert trajectories/episodes for downstream training and benchmarking. Each episode consists of temporally aligned state-action sequences with multimodal observations. Visual observations include rendered RGB images from calibrated cameras (often multi-view) to capture both global context and fine-grained contact-relevant details. Proprioceptive observations include robot joint states (e.g., positions/velocities) and gripper states. Actions are specified in continuous control space (e.g., end-effector or joint-space commands), which makes the dataset compatible with standard imitation learning and policy learning pipelines.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, RoboTwin 2.0 is designed to support scalable training and controlled evaluation of general-purpose policies, particularly for studying cross-task and cross-embodiment generalization under instruction- or goal-conditioned settings.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Model Details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>OpenVLA</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2024</a>)</cite> is a 7B-parameter VLA based on the <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prismatic-7B VLM</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karamcheti et al., 2024</a>)</cite> framework. The architecture’s vision tower employs a fused visual encoder (totaling 600M parameters) constructed by combining two pretrained vision models: <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DINOv2</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oquab et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SigLIP</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhai et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Specifically, input image patches are passed separately through both encoders, and the resulting feature vectors are concatenated channel-wise. These fused visual features are then mapped into the language embedding space via a small 2-layer Multi-Layer Perceptron <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(MLP) projector</span>. The central reasoning engine is a 7B-parameter <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Llama 2</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023</a>)</cite> language model backbone, which processes the interleaved visual tokens and language instructions to predict 7-dimensional robot actions. It features <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">32 Transformer layers</span> with <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a hidden dimension of 4096</span> and <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">32 attention heads</span>. OpenVLA represents robot actions by discretizing them into <span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">256 bins per dimension</span>, treating them as specialized tokens within the LLM’s vocabulary.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>OpenVLA-OFT</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OpenVLA-OFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025</a>)</cite> is a fine-tuning variant of OpenVLA that inherits the same base components. Instead of discretizing actions, OpenVLA-OFT employs a <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">continuous action prediction head</span>—a 2-block MLP ResNet that directly predicts 7-dimensional continuous actions from the LLM’s hidden states via L1 regression. During fine-tuning, OpenVLA-OFT freezes the vision tower and projector and applies <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LoRA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2021</a>)</cite> adapters to the LLM backbone, targeting all linear layers in self-attention and MLP blocks. OpenVLA-OFT+ extends it with <span id="A4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FiLM</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Perez et al., 2018</a>)</cite> for enhanced language grounding. Specifically, FiLM applies learnable affine transformations to the visual features based on the language instruction, enabling the model to modulate visual representations according to task-specific language cues.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>PI0</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">PI0<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite> is a vision-language-action (VLA) model that generates robot action sequences using flow matching. The model employs a dual-expert architecture: a vision-language expert and an action expert. The vision tower uses <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SigLIP So400m/14</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhai et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. The language model is <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PaliGemma</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beyer et al., 2024</a>)</cite> based on Gemma 2B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mesnard et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, with <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">hidden dimension 2048, 18 transformer layers</span>. The action expert is a <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gemma 300M</span> model with hidden dimension 1024, 18 layers. During training, PI0 learns a velocity field <math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> via <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">flow matching</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span>PI0.5</h3>

<div id="A4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">PI0.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2025</a>)</cite> shares the same architectural foundation as PI0 but introduces two key modifications for improved open-world generalization through knowledge insulation. First, instead of providing the robot state as a continuous vector in the suffix, PI0.5 discretizes the state into <span id="A4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">256 bins</span> over <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and incorporates it as discrete tokens in the language prefix. Second, PI0.5 replaces MLP-based timestep fusion with adaptive RMS normalization (<span id="A4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AdaRMSNorm</span>) for timestep conditioning. The timestep embedding is processed through a two-layer MLP with Swish activations to produce a 1024-dimensional condition vector. This condition is injected into the action expert through AdaRMSNorm layers in each of the 18 transformer layers, where AdaRMSNorm dynamically generates scale and shift parameters, which provides more flexible timestep conditioning compared to the MLP fusion approach in PI0.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Projector Similarity</h2>

<figure id="A5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/figures/projector_similarity_cosine.png" id="A5.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:262/234;" width="262" height="234" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Pairwise cosine similarity of flattened MLP parameters for independently initialized projectors. The similarities are nearly zero, suggesting that naive multi-layer alignment with multiple independent projectors learns distinct mapping trajectories, which can induce gradient conflicts and harm final performance.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We flatten the MLP parameters of each independently initialized projector (i.e., <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}</annotation></semantics></math>) and compute the pairwise cosine similarities. As shown in Fig. <a href="#A5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix E Projector Similarity ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, the similarities between different projectors are nearly zero, indicating that naive multi-layer alignment with multiple independent projectors tends to learn distinct mapping trajectories when modeling the transformation from one residual stream to another. This discrepancy can lead to gradient conflicts, which in turn degrades the final performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Why We Need a Nested Sparse-Activation Mechanism to Balance Multiple Alignment Losses</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compute the similarity between the student model OpenVLA-7B and the teacher model VGGT using centered kernel alignment (CKA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cortes et al., 2012</a>)</cite>. As shown in Fig.<a href="#A6.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix F Why We Need a Nested Sparse-Activation Mechanism to Balance Multiple Alignment Losses ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, we observe that the shallow layers of VGGT are more similar to OpenVLA-7B, while the similarity gradually decreases as the depth increases. This finding not only suggests that different layers of VGGT contain semantic information with varying levels of richness, but also indicates that it is easier to align VGGT and OpenVLA-7B at shallow layers. In practice, a shared projector typically learns a mapping that works well for aligning shallow layers; however, it often fails to achieve equally good alignment for deeper layers.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/figures/cka_heatmap.png" id="A6.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:405/564;" width="405" height="564" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="A6.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Layer-wise CKA similarity between OpenVLA-7B and VGGT.<span id="A6.F8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
We compute linear CKA between OpenVLA-7B vision-token representations and VGGT visual features across layers.
Higher values indicate more similar representations. Shallow VGGT layers exhibit higher similarity to OpenVLA-7B, and similarity generally decreases with depth.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To address this multi-layer alignment mismatch, we propose a nested sparse-activation mechanism. The key idea is to let shallow layers activate (and thus update/use) fewer parameters in the projector, and gradually increase the number of activated parameters as the layer depth increases, until reaching the full projector capacity at the deepest layers.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">CKA principle.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CKA measures the similarity between two representation spaces by comparing their induced pairwise similarity structure, and can be viewed as a normalized version of HSIC (Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion). Concretely, suppose we collect representations from one layer of the student model as a matrix <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> and from one layer of the teacher model as <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_{y}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of matched observations (e.g., the same <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> tokens or image regions), while <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> can be different.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A common choice is <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">linear CKA</em>, computed via Gram matrices:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=XX^{\top},\quad L=YY^{\top}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=XX^{\top},\quad L=YY^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">and centering them with the centering matrix <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=I-\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mn>𝟏𝟏</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=I-\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{K}=HKH,\quad\tilde{L}=HLH." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{K}=HKH,\quad\tilde{L}=HLH.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Then CKA is</p>
<table id="A6.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\frac{\langle\tilde{K},\tilde{L}\rangle_{F}}{\|\tilde{K}\|_{F}\,\|\tilde{L}\|_{F}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>CKA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\frac{\langle\tilde{K},\tilde{L}\rangle_{F}}{\|\tilde{K}\|_{F}\,\|\tilde{L}\|_{F}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle A,B\rangle_{F}=\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle A,B\rangle_{F}=\mathrm{tr}(A^{\top}B)</annotation></semantics></math> is the Frobenius inner product.
Equivalently, for centered <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>, linear CKA can be written as:</p>
<table id="A6.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A6.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\frac{\|X^{\top}Y\|_{F}^{2}}{\|X^{\top}X\|_{F}\,\|Y^{\top}Y\|_{F}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>CKA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\frac{\|X^{\top}Y\|_{F}^{2}}{\|X^{\top}X\|_{F}\,\|Y^{\top}Y\|_{F}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.5" class="ltx_p">Importantly, the above formulation does <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.5.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not</em> require <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{x}=d_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{x}=d_{y}</annotation></semantics></math>; it only requires that <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> share the same number of rows <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., aligned observations). Intuitively, CKA compares how similarly the two models organize the same set of examples in representation space, and it is invariant to isotropic scaling (and, in the linear case, robust to orthogonal transformations), making it suitable for cross-model, cross-dimension similarity analysis.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Details of computing CKA similarity between OpenVLA-7B and VGGT.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since OpenVLA-7B and VGGT have different hidden dimensions, we adopt CKA because it can compare representations of different feature dimensions as long as they are evaluated on the same set of samples (tokens/images), i.e., the same number of observations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our implementation, we measure representation similarity between OpenVLA-7B (student) and VGGT (teacher) using <em id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">linear CKA</em> on a held-out set of samples. For each input batch, we extract the vision-token hidden states from selected layers of OpenVLA-7B and the corresponding visual features from selected layers of VGGT. Since the two models have different spatial resolutions and hidden dimensions, we first resample the VGGT features to match the spatial layout of OpenVLA’s vision tokens, then flatten both representations into per-sample feature vectors and concatenate all samples to form matrices <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D_{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D_{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D_{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D_{y}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We then compute linear CKA for every layer pair by constructing and centering Gram matrices <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=XX^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=XX^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=YY^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=YY^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, and reporting the normalized HSIC score <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\langle\tilde{K},\tilde{L}\rangle_{F}/(\|\tilde{K}\|_{F}\|\tilde{L}\|_{F})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>CKA</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>K</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CKA}(X,Y)=\langle\tilde{K},\tilde{L}\rangle_{F}/(\|\tilde{K}\|_{F}\|\tilde{L}\|_{F})</annotation></semantics></math>, which is comparable even when <math id="A6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{x}\neq D_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{x}\neq D_{y}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Per-task Results on LIBERO-Plus</h2>

</div>

</figure>
<figure id="A7.F12" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17951v1/figures/libero_plus_long.png" id="A7.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:481/104;" width="481" height="104" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A7.F12.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="A7.F12.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Per-task success rate (%) on LIBERO-Plus <span id="A7.F12.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long</span> tasks under the seven perturbations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence</h2>

<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Takeaway: shared projector makes cross-layer gradients add constructively</h3>

<div id="A8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section explains why a <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">shared</em> nonlinear projector tends to yield more <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cross-layer coherent</em>
distillation gradients than <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">layer-specific</em> independent projectors in a Pre-LN Transformer.
The argument has two steps:
(i) under Pre-LN <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">residual-smallness</em>, back-propagation through the residual stream is close to identity,
so the gradient at an earlier layer is approximately a superposition of <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">future local</em> distillation gradients;
(ii) the stability of this superposition is governed by <em id="A8.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cross-layer interference</em> terms, and a shared projector
imposes a common operator structure on these terms (up to controlled deviation), whereas Multiple independent projectors do not.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Setup: Pre-LN residual stream, nonlinear projector, and distillation loss</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let the student network be a Pre-LN Transformer written on the residual stream:</p>
<table id="A8.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{h_{l+1}\;=\;h_{l}\;+\;F_{l}\!\left(\mathrm{LN}(h_{l});\theta_{l}\right),\qquad l=0,\dots,L-1}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mi>F</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>LN</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>)</mo><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{h_{l+1}\;=\;h_{l}\;+\;F_{l}\!\left(\mathrm{LN}(h_{l});\theta_{l}\right),\qquad l=0,\dots,L-1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{l}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the (flattened) residual representation at layer <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LN}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>LN</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LN}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is LayerNorm, and <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> are the block parameters.
Define <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{l}:=\mathrm{LN}(h_{l})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>LN</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{l}:=\mathrm{LN}(h_{l})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{l}:=F_{l}(u_{l};\theta_{l})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{l}:=F_{l}(u_{l};\theta_{l})</annotation></semantics></math> so that
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{l+1}=h_{l}+\Delta_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{l+1}=h_{l}+\Delta_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Nonlinear projector.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each distillation layer <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, we attach a two-layer MLP projector
(with input normalization <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LN}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LN</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LN}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>):</p>
<table id="A8.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.E19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle:=W_{2}\,\sigma\!\left(W_{1}\tilde{h}_{l}\right),\qquad\sigma=\mathrm{GELU}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.437em;" width="0.437em"><mi>σ</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>GELU</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=W_{2}\,\sigma\!\left(W_{1}\tilde{h}_{l}\right),\qquad\sigma=\mathrm{GELU},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi=\{W_{1},W_{2}\}</annotation></semantics></math> (and potentially <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LN}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LN</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LN}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> parameters).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Layerwise distillation loss.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the teacher representation used as the distillation target for the student’s layer <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>, selected via a fixed layer mapping.
We define the multi-layer distillation objective:</p>
<table id="A8.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}(\theta,\{\phi_{l}\})\;:=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}}\alpha_{l}\,\ell\!\left(z_{l},t_{l}\right),\qquad z_{l}:=p_{\phi_{l}}(h_{l}(\theta))," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.391em">:=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.247em;" width="0.247em"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}(\theta,\{\phi_{l}\})\;:=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}}\alpha_{l}\,\ell\!\left(z_{l},t_{l}\right),\qquad z_{l}:=p_{\phi_{l}}(h_{l}(\theta)),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is any differentiable similarity loss
(e.g., <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\cos(\cdot,\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\cos(\cdot,\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{l}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{l}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> is the coefficient of the alignment loss; by default, we use uniform (mean) weighting.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.3 </span>Jacobians needed for gradient transport and projector-induced coupling</h3>

<section id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pre-LN residual Jacobian.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Differentiating (<a href="#A8.E17" title="Equation 17 ‣ H.2 Setup: Pre-LN residual stream, nonlinear projector, and distillation loss ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>) yields</p>
<table id="A8.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial h_{l+1}}{\partial h_{l}}\;=\;I+A_{l},\qquad A_{l}:=\frac{\partial F_{l}(u_{l};\theta_{l})}{\partial u_{l}}\,J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{l})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>LN</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial h_{l+1}}{\partial h_{l}}\;=\;I+A_{l},\qquad A_{l}:=\frac{\partial F_{l}(u_{l};\theta_{l})}{\partial u_{l}}\,J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{l}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{l})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>LN</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{l})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the Jacobian of <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LN}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>LN</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LN}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus, for <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&lt;l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&lt;l</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial h_{l}}{\partial h_{i}}\;=\;\prod_{k=1}^{l-i}(I+A_{l-k})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.391em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial h_{l}}{\partial h_{i}}\;=\;\prod_{k=1}^{l-i}(I+A_{l-k}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>

<section id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Projector Jacobian.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x:=W_{1}\tilde{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x:=W_{1}\tilde{h}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\sigma}(x):=\mathrm{diag}(\sigma^{\prime}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\sigma}(x):=\mathrm{diag}(\sigma^{\prime}(x))</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then the Jacobian of (<a href="#A8.E19" title="Equation 19 ‣ Nonlinear projector. ‣ H.2 Setup: Pre-LN residual stream, nonlinear projector, and distillation loss ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>) is</p>

<p id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{\mathrm{LN}_{v}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>LN</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\mathrm{LN}_{v}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> is the Jacobian of <math id="A8.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{LN}_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>LN</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{LN}_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="A8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.4 </span>Exact gradient at an early layer and its superposition approximation</h3>

<div id="A8.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This subsection writes the exact distillation gradient at <math id="A8.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and then states the approximation that removes
deep transport effects under Pre-LN residual-smallness.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, define the local gradient from the distillation loss:</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{l}\;:=\;\nabla_{z_{l}}\,\ell(z_{l},t_{l})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{l}\;:=\;\nabla_{z_{l}}\,\ell(z_{l},t_{l}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">By the chain rule, the gradient at the student layer <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> is:</p>

</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.p2.3" class="ltx_p">For an earlier layer <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&lt;l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&lt;l</annotation></semantics></math>, the gradient is back-propagated through the residual blocks. Note that for a product of matrices <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{l-1}\dots M_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{l-1}\dots M_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the transpose reverses the order to <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{i}^{\top}\dots M_{l-1}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{i}^{\top}\dots M_{l-1}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, we have:</p>
<table id="A8.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS4.p2.4" class="ltx_p">where the product is ordered from <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=i</annotation></semantics></math> (leftmost) to <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l-1</annotation></semantics></math> (rightmost).
Summing over all distillation layers <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\geq i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\geq i</annotation></semantics></math> gives the total gradient at layer <math id="A8.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E27.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nabla_{h_{i}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}\;=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\left(\prod_{k=i}^{l-1}(I+A_{k})^{\top}\right)J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}\,g_{l}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>align</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.391em">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{h_{i}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}\;=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\left(\prod_{k=i}^{l-1}(I+A_{k})^{\top}\right)J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}\,g_{l}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<section id="A8.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.5 </span>Residual-smallness implies near-identity transport</h3>

<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Assumption (Residual-smallness for Pre-LN).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">There exists <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> of interest,</p>
<table id="A8.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|A_{k}\|=\left\|\frac{\partial F_{k}(u_{k};\theta_{k})}{\partial u_{k}}\,J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{k})\right\|\leq\varepsilon." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>LN</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|A_{k}\|=\left\|\frac{\partial F_{k}(u_{k};\theta_{k})}{\partial u_{k}}\,J_{\mathrm{LN}}(h_{k})\right\|\leq\varepsilon.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(28)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lemma 1 (Near-identity transport).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under (<a href="#A8.E28" title="Equation 28 ‣ Assumption (Residual-smallness for Pre-LN). ‣ H.5 Residual-smallness implies near-identity transport ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a>), for any <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&lt;l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&lt;l</annotation></semantics></math>, the back-propagation matrix remains close to the identity:</p>
<table id="A8.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\|\prod_{k=i}^{l-1}(I+A_{k})^{\top}-I\right\|\leq\exp\big((l-i)\varepsilon\big)-1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\|\prod_{k=i}^{l-1}(I+A_{k})^{\top}-I\right\|\leq\exp\big((l-i)\varepsilon\big)-1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For small depth or residuals (i.e., <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(l-i)\varepsilon\ll 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><mo>≪</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(l-i)\varepsilon\ll 1</annotation></semantics></math>), this bound is approximately <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(l-i)\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(l-i)\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Corollary 1 (Gradient is a sum of local distillation gradients, up to transport error).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Substituting the bound from Lemma 1 into (<a href="#A8.E27" title="Equation 27 ‣ H.4 Exact gradient at an early layer and its superposition approximation ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a>), we obtain that the gradient at layer <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is the superposition of future local gradients plus an error term dependent on depth:</p>
<table id="A8.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\nabla_{h_{i}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}\;=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}\,g_{l}\;+\;\mathcal{E}_{i}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>align</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.391em">=</mo><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>α</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\nabla_{h_{i}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{align}}\;=\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}\,g_{l}\;+\;\mathcal{E}_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the error <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded by order <math id="A8.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\!\left(\varepsilon\sum_{l\geq i}(l-i)\,\alpha_{l}\|J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}^{\top}g_{l}\|\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.621em;" width="0.621em"><mi>O</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\!\left(\varepsilon\sum_{l\geq i}(l-i)\,\alpha_{l}\|J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}^{\top}g_{l}\|\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.6 </span>Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive</h3>

<div id="A8.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By Corollary 1, the stability of the early-layer update is controlled by how the terms
<math id="A8.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> interact across distillation layers. We now show that sharing the projector
creates a <em id="A8.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">common operator</em> governing these interactions (up to controlled deviation), yielding a
signal-aligned lower bound on cross-layer interference.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We compare two parameterization strategies for the auxiliary tasks:</p>
<ul id="A8.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multiple independent projectors:</span> each <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> has distinct parameters <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Shared projector:</span> a single set of parameters <math id="A8.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{l}\equiv\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{l}\equiv\phi</annotation></semantics></math> is used for all <math id="A8.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gradient forms and the interference term.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recalling (<a href="#A8.E30" title="Equation 30 ‣ Corollary 1 (Gradient is a sum of local distillation gradients, up to transport error). ‣ H.5 Residual-smallness implies near-identity transport ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a>), the gradient at representation <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a superposition of terms.
Let</p>
<table id="A8.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E31.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="v_{l}\;:=\;J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l},\qquad G\;\approx\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,v_{l}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.391em">≈</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{l}\;:=\;J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})^{\top}g_{l},\qquad G\;\approx\;\sum_{l\in\mathcal{S}:l\geq i}\alpha_{l}\,v_{l}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where the cross terms <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> determine whether different distillation layers reinforce or
cancel each other.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proposition 1 (Cross-layer interference as a bilinear form on teacher-side error signals).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For any <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
