<section id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Error-signal subspace.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let the <em id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">error-signal subspace</em> be</p>
<table id="A8.E34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}\;:=\;\mathrm{span}\{g_{l}:\ l\in\mathcal{S}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\dim(z)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><mi>span</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.778em">:</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mo rspace="0em">dim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}\;:=\;\mathrm{span}\{g_{l}:\ l\in\mathcal{S}\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{\dim(z)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(34)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">All teacher-side signals that affect the student update through distillation lie in <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> by construction.
Accordingly, we will only require geometric regularity of the shared projector on <math id="A8.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">H.6.1 </span><span id="A8.SS6.SSS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference.</span></h4>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The advantage of shared projector is that cross-layer interactions are governed by (approximately) a <em id="A8.SS6.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">single</em> operator
on the teacher-side error signals. The following assumptions control how the shared projector Jacobian varies along
the residual stream, enabling us to relate <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{ab}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{ab}</annotation></semantics></math> to a fixed PSD reference operator.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Assumption (Bounded residual increments).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">There exists <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all layers <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|h_{l+1}-h_{l}\|_{2}=\|\Delta_{l}\|_{2}\leq\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h_{l+1}-h_{l}\|_{2}=\|\Delta_{l}\|_{2}\leq\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Assumption (Projector Jacobian Lipschitz).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">There exists <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{J}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>J</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{J}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y</annotation></semantics></math> in the bounded feature domain,</p>

<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lemma 2 (Cross-layer Jacobian closeness under residual dynamics).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under (<a href="#A8.E35" title="Equation 35 ‣ Assumption (Bounded residual increments). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">35</span></a>) and (<a href="#A8.E36" title="Equation 36 ‣ Assumption (Projector Jacobian Lipschitz). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>), for any <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&lt;b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&lt;b</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{b})-J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{a})\|_{2}\leq L_{J}\,(b-a)\,\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>J</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{b})-J_{p_{\phi}}(h_{a})\|_{2}\leq L_{J}\,(b-a)\,\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To convert Jacobian closeness into a statement about alignment, we introduce an <em id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">on-subspace</em>
near-isometry requirement on the teacher-side signals that actually occur.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Assumption (Near-isometry on the error-signal subspace).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a reference layer <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{l}\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{l}\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{h}:=h_{\bar{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>:=</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{h}:=h_{\bar{l}}</annotation></semantics></math>, define</p>

<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Assume there exist constants <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> has condition number at most <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}</annotation></semantics></math> when restricted to <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lemma 3 (Approximate inner-product preservation on <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>).</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under (<a href="#A8.E39" title="Equation 39 ‣ Assumption (Near-isometry on the error-signal subspace). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">39</span></a>), for all <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y\in\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E40.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\big|x^{\top}My-c\,x^{\top}y\big|\;\leq\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|x\|_{2}^{2}+\|y\|_{2}^{2}}{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.280em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\big|x^{\top}My-c\,x^{\top}y\big|\;\leq\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|x\|_{2}^{2}+\|y\|_{2}^{2}}{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(40)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Proof sketch.</span>
Use the polarization identity
<math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{\top}My=\frac{1}{4}\big((x+y)^{\top}M(x+y)-(x-y)^{\top}M(x-y)\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\top}My=\frac{1}{4}\big((x+y)^{\top}M(x+y)-(x-y)^{\top}M(x-y)\big)</annotation></semantics></math>
and apply the quadratic bounds (<a href="#A8.E39" title="Equation 39 ‣ Assumption (Near-isometry on the error-signal subspace). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">39</span></a>) to <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\pm y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>±</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\pm y</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Moreover, if <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a},g_{b}\in\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a},g_{b}\in\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, then by Lemma 3,</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}\;\geq\;c\,g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}\;-\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|g_{a}\|_{2}^{2}+\|g_{b}\|_{2}^{2}}{2}\;-\;|\Delta_{ab}|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>share</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{share}}\;\geq\;c\,g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}\;-\;\eta c\cdot\frac{\|g_{a}\|_{2}^{2}+\|g_{b}\|_{2}^{2}}{2}\;-\;|\Delta_{ab}|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(44)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Interpretation.</span>
When (i) the teacher error signals are consistent across layers (<math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> positive and not too small),
(ii) the shared projector is near-isometric on <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> (small <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>),
and (iii) adjacent-layer Jacobians are close (small <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|E_{l}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|E_{l}\|</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., small <math id="A8.SS6.SSS1.Px6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(|l-\bar{l}|\delta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(|l-\bar{l}|\delta)</annotation></semantics></math>),
the cross-layer interference term is biased toward being non-destructive and often constructive.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem H.1</span></span><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Shared projector induces coherent cross-layer interference under Pre-LN transport)<span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Consider the Pre-LN student (<a href="#A8.E17" title="Equation 17 ‣ H.2 Setup: Pre-LN residual stream, nonlinear projector, and distillation loss ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>) with multi-layer distillation (<a href="#A8.E20" title="Equation 20 ‣ Layerwise distillation loss. ‣ H.2 Setup: Pre-LN residual stream, nonlinear projector, and distillation loss ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>).
Under residual-smallness (<a href="#A8.E28" title="Equation 28 ‣ Assumption (Residual-smallness for Pre-LN). ‣ H.5 Residual-smallness implies near-identity transport ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a>), the gradient at an earlier representation <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>
admits the superposition form (<a href="#A8.E30" title="Equation 30 ‣ Corollary 1 (Gradient is a sum of local distillation gradients, up to transport error). ‣ H.5 Residual-smallness implies near-identity transport ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a>).
For the shared projector parameterization (<math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{l}\equiv\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>≡</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{l}\equiv\phi</annotation></semantics></math>), assume bounded residual increments
(<a href="#A8.E35" title="Equation 35 ‣ Assumption (Bounded residual increments). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">35</span></a>), projector Jacobian Lipschitzness (<a href="#A8.E36" title="Equation 36 ‣ Assumption (Projector Jacobian Lipschitz). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>), and near-isometry on
the error-signal subspace (<a href="#A8.E39" title="Equation 39 ‣ Assumption (Near-isometry on the error-signal subspace). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">39</span></a>).
Then for any <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,b\geq i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,b\geq i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a},g_{b}\in\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a},g_{b}\in\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>, the cross-layer interference
term <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> in (<a href="#A8.E32" title="Equation 32 ‣ Gradient forms and the interference term. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>) satisfies the shared projector decomposition
(<a href="#A8.E42" title="Equation 42 ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">42</span></a>) with deviation bounded by (<a href="#A8.E43" title="Equation 43 ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">43</span></a>), and furthermore
admits the signal-aligned lower bound (<a href="#A8.E44" title="Equation 44 ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">44</span></a>).
Consequently, when teacher-side error signals are positively correlated across layers (large <math id="A8.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>) and the
controlled-deviation terms are small, shared projector gradients exhibit reduced destructive interference and higher
cross-layer coherence in the superposition (<a href="#A8.E31" title="Equation 31 ‣ Gradient forms and the interference term. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">H.6.2 </span><span id="A8.SS6.SSS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound.</span></h4>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For Multiple independent projectors, the cross term becomes</p>
<table id="A8.E45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(45)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which does not reduce to a single PSD form <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a}^{\top}(JJ^{\top})g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>J</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a}^{\top}(JJ^{\top})g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> and therefore admits no analogue of
(<a href="#A8.E40" title="Equation 40 ‣ Lemma 3 (Approximate inner-product preservation on 𝒢). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">40</span></a>) or (<a href="#A8.E44" title="Equation 44 ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">44</span></a>) without additional coupling assumptions.
A generic upper bound is</p>
<table id="A8.E46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{|\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{multi}}|\;\leq\;\|g_{a}\|_{2}\|g_{b}\|_{2}\,\|J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})\|_{2}\,\|J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})\|_{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>multi</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{|\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{multi}}|\;\leq\;\|g_{a}\|_{2}\|g_{b}\|_{2}\,\|J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})\|_{2}\,\|J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})\|_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(46)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">but this bound does not preclude sign flips (destructive interference) since the bilinear form
<math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> is not constrained to be PSD or even symmetric.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Empirical specialization and orthogonalization.</span>
In our experiments, we observe a consistent “decoupling” behavior: as training proceeds and the per-layer alignment losses saturate, different projectors tend to rotate their effective Jacobian row spaces into near-orthogonal subspaces. Concretely, if we measure the pairwise similarity between projector weights (or
their local linearizations), e.g., <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos\!\left(\mathrm{vec}(W_{a}),\mathrm{vec}(W_{b})\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.216em;" width="1.216em"><mi>cos</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\!\left(\mathrm{vec}(W_{a}),\mathrm{vec}(W_{b})\right)</annotation></semantics></math> for linear heads
or an analogous metric based on <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{p_{\phi_{l}}}(h_{l})</annotation></semantics></math>, the values decrease toward (and remain close to) zero in the early stage after training has stabilized, and this behavior persists consistently until the end of training (The visualization results are provided in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Projector Similarity ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> (Fig.<a href="#A5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix E Projector Similarity ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).).
This indicates that, rather than enforcing a shared representation geometry
across layers, independent heads can absorb layer-specific discrepancies by specializing into mutually
orthogonal directions, which suppresses cross-layer coupling in (<a href="#A8.E45" title="Equation 45 ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">45</span></a>).
In Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Residual-dynamical view: multi-layer alignment should be cone-to-cone, yet learned projectors decouple. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (top), we show the cosine similarity between the gradients induced by different alignment losses at an early layer (the projector between the vision tower and the LLM backbone) during the early stage of training and the mid-to-late stage.
For the <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> layers, we compute the pairwise cosine similarities among their gradients. The visualization shows that the gradients in the early stage are nearly perfectly orthogonal, indicating substantial training fluctuations; in the mid-to-late stage, this low cosine similarity persists.
In Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Residual-dynamical view: multi-layer alignment should be cone-to-cone, yet learned projectors decouple. ‣ 3.2 The Gradient-Conflict of Multi-Layer Alignment ‣ 3 Theoretical Framework: Residual Dynamics and Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (bottom), we visualize the corresponding results for <span id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>. From the very early stage of training to the mid-to-late stage, the shared-projector mechanism in <span id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span> keeps the gradients induced by different alignment losses consistently aligned. This directional consistency holds throughout training, and the resulting mutual reinforcement among gradients contributes to the superior performance of <span id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold">ROCKET</span>.
Specifically, Fig. <a href="#A8.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Consequence for gradient stability. ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> shows the gradient similarities in the early stage of training, while Fig. <a href="#A8.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ Consequence for gradient stability. ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> shows the gradient similarities in the mid-to-late stage.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As a consequence, even when the teacher error signals are correlated across layers (i.e., <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{a}^{\top}g_{b}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>),
the induced student-side gradients <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> can become weakly correlated because the interaction matrix
<math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{p_{\phi_{a}}}(h_{a})J_{p_{\phi_{b}}}(h_{b})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> itself shrinks in the relevant directions. In practice, this
often yields a small average cross term <math id="A8.SS6.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{multi}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mi>multi</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\langle v_{a},v_{b}\rangle_{\mathrm{multi}}]</annotation></semantics></math> and can even
lead to destructive interference when the effective interaction changes sign across mini-batches.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS6.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Consequence for gradient stability.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS6.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS6.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Plugging (<a href="#A8.E44" title="Equation 44 ‣ Proposition 2 (Shared projector cross terms decompose into a common PSD part plus deviation). ‣ H.6.1 Case 1 (Shared projector): a common PSD operator governs cross-layer interference. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">44</span></a>) (shared projector) into (<a href="#A8.E32" title="Equation 32 ‣ Gradient forms and the interference term. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>) shows that the second summation
in (<a href="#A8.E32" title="Equation 32 ‣ Gradient forms and the interference term. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>) admits a <em id="A8.SS6.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">signal-aligned</em> lower bound (up to controlled errors),
while Multiple independent projectors admit only the trivial magnitude bound (<a href="#A8.E46" title="Equation 46 ‣ H.6.2 Case 2 (Multiple independent projectors): lack of a uniform constructive lower bound. ‣ H.6 Shared projector makes cross-layer interference constructive ‣ Appendix H Analysis: Why Shared Projectors Increase Cross-Layer Gradient Coherence ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">46</span></a>).
Thus, under the same transport approximation of Corollary 1, shared projector gradients
tend to exhibit higher cross-layer coherence and reduced destructive interference, consistent with empirical observations.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Details of Layer Selection Strategies</h2>

<section id="A9.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.1 </span>Similarity-based Layer Selection</h3>

<figure id="A9.F15" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17951v1/layer_selection_final.svg" id="A9.F15.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/283;" width="405" height="283"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A9.F15.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 15</span>: </span><span id="A9.F15.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A9.F15.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Similarity-based layer selection strategies.</span>
We evaluate two criteria for selecting alignment layers:
<span id="A9.F15.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sim-1</span> (left) measures 10-layer window similarity by computing cosine similarity between layer <math id="A9.F15.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>’s input and layer <math id="A9.F15.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i{+}9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i{+}9</annotation></semantics></math>’s output;
<span id="A9.F15.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sim-2</span> (right) measures single-layer similarity between each layer’s input and output.
For each criterion, we select 10 layers with either highest similarity (<span id="A9.F15.9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top</span>, green squares) or lowest similarity (<span id="A9.F15.9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Last</span>, orange triangles).
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A9.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A9.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ I.1 Similarity-based Layer Selection ‣ Appendix I Details of Layer Selection Strategies ‣ ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> shows that VGGT (24 layers, top row) and VLA (32 layers, bottom row) reveal distinct similarity distributions across the network depth. Lower similarity indicates greater information transformation, potentially identifying more informative layers for alignment.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>Detailed layer selection for multi-layer alignment. We show the aligned layer indices for both the student VLA visual backbone and the teacher VGGT model. For OpenVLA, we count the projector between vision tower and LLM as a layer so there are total 33 indices in our default setting. The selected layers are sorted in ascending order for both VLA and VGGT.
<sup id="A9.T10.10" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A9.T10.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup> For OpenVLA (32 layers, or 33 including the projector), we select layers uniformly using indices 2–18 plus the last layer.
<sup id="A9.T10.11" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A9.T10.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup> For PI0 and PI0.5 (18 layers), since layer 18 coincides with the last layer, we instead select indices 2–10 plus the last layer.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
